title: UK eInvoicing Roadmap: What's Fixed for April 2029, and What Isn't
summary: UK VAT invoices must be structured eInvoices from April 1, 2029. HMRC’s roadmap sets one date with no threshold, confirms Peppol, and leaves the standard open.
body_markdown:
The UK will require businesses to issue and receive VAT invoices as structured eInvoices from April 1, 2029. The government[confirmed the mandate in November 2025](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/promoting-electronic-invoicing-across-uk-businesses-and-the-public-sector/outcome/promoting-electronic-invoicing-across-uk-businesses-and-the-public-sector-consultation-response) . It chose a decentralized model, and named Peppol as the core interoperability network in June 2026. Invoices travel between businesses over the Peppol network, through certified service providers called Access Points, rather than through a government platform. The invoice standard is not settled. HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) says it will build on established international standards and will consult on the proposed UK standards in Spring 2027, which points to EN 16931 and Peppol BIS Billing 3.0. It is not introducing real-time reporting alongside the mandate.


## **What changed**


On October 28, 2026, HMRC and the Department for Business and Trade published the[Roadmap for eInvoicing implementation](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/e-invoicing-implementation-roadmap/roadmap-for-e-invoicing-implementation) , together with a[policy paper on eInvoicing requirements](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/vat-electronic-invoicing/e-invoicing-requirements) detailing the enabling legislation. The roadmap settles five points:


- **A PDF is not an eInvoice.** Today, VAT Notice 700/63 accepts both structured formats such as XML and unstructured ones such as PDF. From April 1, 2029, only structured data counts, which also rules out word-processed documents, JPEG images and HTML invoices.


- **One date, no phasing.** April 1, 2029 applies to everyone in scope, with no turnover threshold.


- **Scope follows the VAT invoice.** VAT-registered businesses must issue an eInvoice wherever they must issue a VAT invoice today. Anyone required to receive a VAT invoice, including public bodies, must be able to receive one. Non-established businesses registered for UK VAT are treated like UK businesses. B2C, cross-border, and exempt supplies are out of scope.


- **Receiving starts on the same date** as issuing.


- HMRC will become the UK Peppol Authority. The function currently sits within the NHS Supply Chain. HMRC, as the UK Peppol Authority, can publish UK-specific requirements for software providers and Access Points. The government has not yet decided whether it needs any.


The roadmap also sets the sequence:


**Date** **Milestone** **Status**


Spring 2027 Enabling powers in Finance Bill 2026-27 Conditional on Parliament


Spring 2027 Technical consultation on standards and Access Point certification Published plan


Oct 2027 – Apr 2028 Key requirements published Published plan


Apr 2028 – Apr 2029 Communications campaign, preparation, testing and onboarding Published plan


Apr 1, 2029 VAT eInvoicing takes effect Published, not yet in force


Several points are still open. HMRC plans to base penalties on the existing VAT invoicing penalty framework “as far as possible,” but has published no amounts. Secondary legislation may not be completed until autumn 2028 or early 2029. Exemptions will be tightly defined and limited, and the government is developing one for digitally excluded VAT-registered persons, with details due by April 2028. Northern Ireland is not separately addressed.


## **What it means**


The roadmap gives businesses a fixed target and at least 12 months between final requirements and go-live. HMRC says there is no need to start implementing before the detailed requirements are published. That is right for build work. It is not right for the decisions that take the longest: which entities and invoice flows are in scope, and which provider connects each of them to Peppol.


Three groups should pay closest attention:


- **Software providers and platforms.** If you issue invoices on behalf of customers, the roadmap puts the obligation on the VAT-registered business and does not say how it is discharged when someone else issues for them. HMRC has said it will clarify the legal position of software providers. Separately, Access Point providers must be certified to operate on the Peppol network, and whether the UK adds its own accreditation requirements is still undecided.


- **Anyone with a view on eReporting.** A separate[consultation](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/e-invoicing-digital-reporting/e-invoicing-digital-reporting-consultation-on-the-future-use-of-e-invoicing-digital-reporting) , open until January 20, 2027, asks whether HMRC could later access selected eInvoice data. No model has been chosen, so now is the time to shape it.


- **Anyone registered for UK VAT, wherever they are based.** HMRC says it will treat non-established taxable persons the same as UK businesses, so a UK-to-UK supply by an overseas seller registered for UK VAT needs an eInvoice when the customer is a VAT-registered business. Scope follows VAT registration rather than establishment, which catches sellers with no UK entity.


B2G invoicing in the UK is mandatory for NHS suppliers. It has been a contractual requirement since the Department of Health's NHS eProcurement Strategy of May 2014, which mandates GS1 coding and Peppol messaging through the NHS Standard Contract. Public bodies must also accept EN 16931 eInvoices under section 67 of the Procurement Act 2023, an obligation that sits on the buyer.


[Invopop covers UK B2G](https://invopop.com/coverage/united-kingdom) . You can send Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 invoices in UBL and receive both UBL and CII, validated against EN 16931 and the Peppol BIS 3.0 CIUS rules, from a single integration built on the open-source GOBL format.


The technical requirements for 2029 are not published yet. The Spring 2027 consultation covers standards and Access Point certification, and the key requirements land between October 2027 and April 2028. We will expand coverage as they are confirmed.
